Description: The 118-acre sports park in Windsor, CO, will feature outdoor fields, professional stadium, collegiate stadium, athlete dormitory, sports bubble, clubhouse and first hotel ready for play and stay. Developer is in negotiations to bring a professional soccer team to play at the site and may also include a minor league baseball team. Plans call for the main stadium to have sporting event seating of 2,800 with another 3,200 for standing room. He said the venue will hold up to 20,000 people for concerts. The project also will include more than 20 baseball/softball and multisport fields as well as a Miracle Field for special-needs athletes.
Status_Update__c:
Hensel Phelps is the GC for the project. HP won the construction management for the project back in December. I spoke with the chief estimator for the project Ryan Montoya on 2/4. HP is also involved on the developer side and has invested in the project so they have a lot of decision-making power with the owner. I told him we would be interested in the AV for the project . The project is currently on a bit of a hold due to COVID but he anticipates some meetings in the next few weeks, and with COVID concerns hopefully dwindling over time, that they will be up and moving again soon. He said once they have a more defined picture he is going to put me in contact with the owners rep that also is an HP guy. He said they know they are going to need things like scoreboards and other digital displays but doesn’t know much other than some preliminary budgeting. I let him know that that is absolutely something we can help with – giving equipment and technology options that fit within their budget. 

Reached out to Casey Katofsky on LinkedIn on 8/24. He let me know that they are still in planning but once a contractor is on board they will know more.

Status_Update__c:
11/10 -We had our first SHU game night. Most was great and of course Sean was great. 

I had to help him out with a few things. We had an issue with a cat cable inside the east facing belly that was resolved with a reseat of the cable. We also replaced a mod on the west facing belly and locally resolved another mod issue on the some display. 

Bigger issue, we have started to see the reemergence of the barge flicker on half of all 4 faces again. This seems to be a home run issue. Please let me know how we can work to get this fixed. We have a busy week this week but the next few have some dark periods. 

As well, Sean needed a lot of help from me when it came to the actual handling of the hardware. Taking the mods off, finding the data ports, and troubleshooting the issues, I have also seen that he may not be very familiar with the Nova menu structure or hardware we have onsite. Also, I would love for both Sean and Kurt to be making sure to do building walks at least an hour before event doors to identify any small issues that need to be addressed. We have seen a few simple brightness issues that I have had to address or one of the engineers has had to address themselves.

Please let me know if we can set up some trainings on site with more of your team to get these on site hands up to speed on what we have here and how to remedy issues when they arise. Normal setups such as making sure all signs have power and content has been no issue at all. I really enjoy having Sean and Kurt here and I want to make sure he is given all the tools and knowledge to get this all done.

Name: Worcester Red Sox (Boston Minor League Team)
Description: The Triple-A Int'l League Pawtucket Red Sox and the city of Worcester have "signed an agreement that clears the way" for the team to move there and play in a ballpark that will be "built on the former Wyman-Gordon property near Kelley Square," according to Nick Kotsopoulos of the Worcester TELEGRAM & GAZETTE. Worcester City Manager Edward Augustus Jr. said that the plan "includes a large-scale redevelopment of 18 acres of largely vacant and blighted property in the Kelley Square area that will add to the ongoing revitalization of the Canal District and transform that part of the city." In addition to construction of a 10,000-seat multi-use ballpark, at an estimated cost of $86-90M, the deal "includes a development blueprint" that calls for $90M in "private development for 225 market-rate apartments, a 150-room hotel, a second boutique hotel consisting of about 100-110 rooms overlooking the ballpark, and 65,000 square feet of retail/restaurants." City officials said that all of that "would be done in the first phase" of the project by March '21. The second phase of the project "would include 200,000 square feet of residential, office and/or mixed-use development." The total cost of the overall development project "has been pegged" at about $240M. The ballpark will be "named Polar Park, marking the involvement of Polar Beverages of Worcester." Augustus said that he will "seek authorization to have the city borrow" $100.8M -- $70.6M in "general obligation bonds for the cost of the ballpark, land acquisition, culvert work, capitalized interest and borrowing costs," and another $30.2M in bonds that will be covered by the baseball team’s annual rent payment for the ballpark (Worcester TELEGRAM & GAZETTE, 8/18).
Status_Update__c: verbal commitment

Name: New York Road Runners Half Marathon 2020
Status_Update__c:
3-10-20:
At New York Road Runners, the welfare of our running community is always our top priority.  Due to the rapidly developing coronavirus (COVID-19) situation, the NYC Half, scheduled for Sunday, March 15, and the accompanying Rising New York Road Runners youth event, have been canceled.  We appreciate the support of New York City officials through this complicated decision-making process.   
 
We know this is a challenging time for everyone, and the cancellation of the NYC Half is disappointing news to many, but the resources necessary to organize an event with 25,000 runners on the streets of Brooklyn and Manhattan have become strained during this difficult period.  Over the past week the NYRR team worked hard to adjust plans, implementing modifications and accommodations to alleviate crowding and facilitate social distancing.  Unfortunately, it has become clear that we will be unable to proceed in the manner that our runners have come to expect at NYRR events, where the safety and security of our runners, volunteers, staff, partners, and spectators are our main concern.
 
Due to this force majeure cancellation, we will no longer require your company’s services for the 2020 NYC Half. We will be in touch over the next few days to discuss specific details pertaining to services already rendered.
 
We value our relationship and appreciate your understanding in this matter. We look forward to working together on future events.
 
For the latest updates from NYRR on race events, group training, community programing, and NYRR RUNCENTER classes and special events, visit nyrr.org.






As in my other NY Road Runner items, we are looking at upgrading and changing scopes for each of their races.
